title: Build light-space particle transmittance map (R16) via compute
purpose: Generate a deep-shadow-like 2D transmittance (light-space) texture each frame to approximate self-shadowing for the mesh particle cloud.

steps.detail: Create an R16_SFLOAT 2D image (DSM_SIZE, DSM_SIZE), usage: STORAGE | SAMPLED | TRANSFER_DST. Create storage and sampled views; sampler with clamp and linear filter.
At frame start, transition to GENERAL and clear to transmittance=1 (white) with compute or vkCmdClearColorImage.

Add shaders/mesh_dsm_build.comp: for each pixel, march along light ray through the particle cloud bounds (use lightView/proj), sample particle density proxy (e.g., screen-space splat accumulation or a particle buffer read + projected footprint) and accumulate optical depth; write exp(-tau) to the image.
Bind LightUBO and particle buffer; dispatch over DSM_SIZE in tiles. Use Sync2 barriers before mesh shading samples it.

acceptance: DSM image created and updated per frame; average transmittance < 1.0 when particles present
No validation errors; image layout transitions correct
notes: Keep the marching cheap: small fixed steps across the cloud depth; or rasterize projected particle contributions into a temporary light-space buffer as a proxy for density.
